newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Colombo auction low grown tea prices ease.
newsitem.headline: Colombo auction low grown tea prices ease.

text.p: Prices of low grown teas, the mainstay of the Colombo auction, eased on Wednesday as Middle Eastern buyers held back while high growns firmed, brokers said.
"Considering it has been the fasting period in most Middle Eastern countries there was no real hurry for buyers to pick up tea," said a Forbes and Walker broker.
The large volume of low grown teas may also have contributed to the fall in prices, he added.
Prices of low growns, which had been expected to come down since they were considered high compared to high growns and ex-estate teas, should stabilise soon, brokers said.
Among high growns, better Western BOP/BOPFs were 4-6 rupees dearer, sometimes more following quality, while Nuwara Eliyas were up sharply on special enquiry, they said.

The anticipated gross sale average for the 4.5 million kg on offer rose to about 103.50 rupees per kg from 102.98 last week. The next auction is on February 11-12 with 5.1 million kg on offer. (1$=57.64 rupees) --Colombo newsroom (941) 434319
